### Executive Summary

A security report published by Sophos indicates that identity-based attacks are responsible for 85% of ransomware incidents targeting the education sector. The findings highlight compromised credentials and identity exploitation as the predominant vector for ransomware deployments in educational environments.

Further operational details and organizational impacts beyond these statistical figures remain unconfirmed in the provided source material.

### Technical Impact & Root Cause

The root cause of these ransomware deployments stems from identity-based intrusion vectors, where threat actors leverage compromised user credentials, weak authentication mechanisms, or privilege abuse to gain initial entry. 

Once initial access via compromised identities is achieved, adversaries deploy ransomware across internal networks, impacting institutional operations and data accessibility. Specific vulnerabilities exploited or technical lateral movement techniques were not detailed in the source material.

### Mitigation & IOCs

Organizations in the education sector should focus on identity protection controls, including strict access management and multi-factor authentication, to reduce the risk of identity-based compromise. Additional specific mitigation steps were not detailed in the source content.
